answer: To resist sybils, an agent economy can require every new identity to lock collateral that is slashed if peers catch it faking work. Sybils multiply one persona into thousands, but the bond multiplies with each clone, so a flood of fake agents costs a matching pile of deposits. Reputation grows like a vine only through verifiable transactions, and each fresh inlet into the network must post real stake before earning anything. That up-front cost turns the voyage of every fake identity into a guaranteed loss, collapsing the attack to its economic floor.
